title: subscribe_events unfold state=None drops pending data silently
description: The subscribe_events unfold closure begins with: let SseStreamState { .. } = state?; When state is None the ? operator returns None from the closure, terminating the stream. This is the intended termination path and does not panic. However, once SseFrameTooLarge is returned the closure passes state=None as the new state, which means on the next poll the stream immediately terminates via the state? shortcircuit. This is correct. The actual issue: after a transport error (Some(Err(e))) the closure returns Some((Err(...), Some(state))) — the stream continues. A caller who ignores the error and keeps polling will re-enter the loop, call stream.next().await again on an already-errored stream, and likely get repeated errors or a hang. The error case should return state=None to force stream termination after a transport error, consistent with the SseFrameTooLarge handling.
